Nap after the Rome turnaround to pay back last night before another 05:00 start tomorrow.

conflicts.statement: Off duty at 19:40 local on 03/11 after a 15h30 duty from Singapore, then report 05:40 local on 04/11 — 10h00 between duties at home base, which is less than both 12 hours and the length of the preceding duty. With an 85-minute commute each way the actual sleep opportunity in bed is about 6 hours, taken while my body is still part-way on Singapore time.
options: Ask crewing to move the MAD-FCO report later or swap the 04/11 turnaround off
Stay in an airport hotel on the night of 03/11 to buy back roughly 2h30 of sleep opportunity
File a fatigue report and decline the 04/11 duty if the sleep does not materialise
Treat 04/11 as a discretion-free day: no extensions, and expect to be at the low point around the 05:40 FCO departure

conflicts.statement: Second consecutive early start — 05:40 report on 04/11 followed by a 05:00 standby start on 05/11, then 05:05 on 09/11. Each one means waking at 03:00-04:15 local, inside the 02:00-06:00 body-clock trough, on the back of a long-haul block.
options: Ask for the 05/11 standby to be a home standby rather than airport, so the wake-up moves later
Request the early starts be grouped away from the Singapore pairings at the next roster build
Protect the 04/11 afternoon nap as non-negotiable
Flag the accumulation to the operator's FRM team as a rostering pattern, not a one-off

conflicts.statement: Four flight duty periods of 15h30 report-to-off-duty (29/10, 31/10, 01/11, 03/11) on the Singapore rotations, well beyond any unaugmented maximum FDP.
options: Confirm with crewing that all four are rostered as augmented crew with in-flight rest
Confirm which bunk/rest class applies and agree the rest split at briefing
Take the first in-flight rest period on the eastbound legs and the second on westbound

conflicts.statement: DXB-MAD reports at 21:40 local and runs to 04:40 local — the entire duty sits inside the 02:00-06:00 window, and it is the second night duty in three days after the 21/10 outbound.
options: Take the 23/10 afternoon nap in Dubai as planned, not optional
Agree controlled rest on the flight deck with the other pilot before top of descent
Expect a low point on approach into Madrid and brief for it

conflicts.statement: BOG-MAD is a 12h15 duty finishing at 02:30 local Madrid, landing at the circadian low after a westward nightstop where the body is still on home time — the arrival is effectively 08:30 on my internal clock but I will have been awake since 07:00 Bogotá.
options: Take both the Bogotá night sleep and the pre-duty nap
Plan in-flight rest early enough in the sector to cover the descent
Arrange a lift home rather than driving after the 02:30 arrival

conflicts.statement: A 9-hour standby from 05:00 local, with a callout at any point counting toward the subsequent FDP — a late callout on 05/11 would push the day well past the sleep I have budgeted for the Bogotá departure on 06/11.
options: Confirm how standby time counts toward FDP under the operator's scheme
If called out late in the window, ask crewing to protect the 06/11 report
Keep the 05/11 afternoon nap even if released early

conflicts.statement: The roster prints report 1h30 before STD on all long-haul sectors but only 1h00 before STD on the FCO and LHR turnarounds (04/11 and 09/11), and does not state the reporting rule anywhere. I have used the printed report times as given.
options: Confirm the short-haul reporting offset with crewing before 04/11
If the true offset is 1h30, the 04/11 report moves to 05:10 local and the rest shortfall above gets worse by 30 minutes
